Amount is not applicable: no fare or route breach appears on these records (actual distance is 0.1 km shorter than optimal, and the fare is a fixed quote that mileage does not change), so there is nothing to compute [F1][F2].

Facts for the human reviewer to check: any telemetry or in-app safety report associated with the 21:22–21:34 window; the full chat thread beyond F3/F4 (only two messages are in the file) for any report made contemporaneously by voice or outside the app; and the driver's statement at F5, which is a user-submitted statement and therefore the weakest evidence class in the file. Profiles: rider 3.5 years, rating 4.82, 0 disputes in 90 days; driver 3.6 years, 345 trips in 90 days, rating 4.5, 0 disputes and 0 upheld — these are context only and per policy cannot decide the incident, and on this record none of them supports any account-level or fare action against either party [F6][F7][SAFE-2].

claims.assertion: This is a safety dispute: the rider reports speeding, hard braking and overtaking on the shoulder throughout the trip, and states she was scared and felt unsafe — an allegation of dangerous driving that Ryde's policy routes to human review rather than an automated fare ruling.

The rider is a long-standing, credible complainant: account age 3.5 years, rating 4.82, zero disputes in the last 90 days — so her report of feeling unsafe deserves a genuine human review rather than dismissal.

The driver's conduct record is clean (3.6 years, 4.5 rating, 0 disputes, 0 upheld in 90 days), so there is no basis to ask for an account-level sanction against him; the request is limited to escalating the safety report for human handling.

The trip was a fixed-fare RydeX trip of 8.6 km estimated / 14 min estimated, and the recorded actual distance (8.5 km) and duration (12.8 min) show no route deviation or overrun, so no fare refund is claimed here — the rider's remedy sought is the safety escalation itself.

weaknesses: No objective record supports the speeding/braking/shoulder-overtaking allegation: the only system facts are F1 and F2, which show the trip was slightly shorter and faster than the optimal route and estimate (8.5 km vs 8.6 km; 12.8 min vs 14 min), and no speed, harsh-braking or shoulder-use data exists in the fact table.

The driver's written statement (F5) denies the allegation and says the rider never complained during the trip; the chat log (F3, F4) contains only pickup logistics, so there is no contemporaneous in-app complaint from the rider.
The rider's own account (F6) is a profile fact only, and profile facts cannot by themselves establish that the safety incident occurred.
The rider has no fare facts (get_fare_facts returned none for this dispute type), so even a secondary fare-based remedy cannot be quantified.

claims.assertion: The rider's account of speeding is not corroborated by any system record: the trip was completed in 12.8 min against an estimate of 14 min (F2), i.e. no time was cut to suggest excessive speed. No gps, traffic or timeline fact in the case file records a speed, harsh-braking or shoulder-driving event.

The route actually driven was slightly shorter than optimal — 8.5 km vs 8.6 km optimal (-1%) (F1) — which is consistent with a normal, direct and lawful run rather than the erratic driving described; there are no off-route segments in the fact table.

The rider never raised any safety concern at the time: the only chats are the rider's 21:18 pickup message and the driver's 21:19 arrival reply (F3, F4), and no threat/abuse message exists in the thread.
The driver's account that the rider was on the phone throughout and never complained (F5) is consistent with the absence of any in-app complaint during the 12.8-minute trip (F2, F3, F4).

The driver has 3.6 years on the platform, 345 trips in 90 days, rating 4.5, and zero disputes and zero upheld disputes in 90 days (F7); the rider likewise has zero disputes (F6). This supports leaving the fare and account status unchanged rather than penalising the driver.

weaknesses: The dispute type is 'safety' and a dangerous-driving allegation engages SAFE-2, which routes to escalate; the case file contains no telemetry (no speed, braking or lane-position facts) by which the driver can positively prove his driving was safe, so the driver cannot fully rebut the rider's account from the record.

The rider's complaint is contemporaneous in the ticket and the driver's only rebuttal is his own statement (F5), which under the system-record-priority rule is the weakest class of evidence; there is no gps fact covering the disputed driving behaviour to contradict the rider, unlike F1/F2 which speak only to route and duration.

F7 shows the driver's rating is 4.5, the lowest rating figure in the file compared with the rider's 4.82 (F6); the other side will argue this shows a pattern of poorer ride quality, even though there are zero prior disputes or upheld complaints against him.

points.response: Conceded only as to the record: no fact in the file measures speed or braking, so F1/F2 neither prove the rider's account nor disprove it — and that evidential gap is precisely why a dangerous-driving allegation goes to human review under SAFE-2 rather than being auto-dismissed.

RD-1 governs route choice, not driving manner: F1 (8.5 km vs 8.6 km optimal) is silent on speed, braking and shoulder use, and the rider's complaint was never about the route, so the absence of off-route segments does not answer SAFE-2.

The absence of an in-app message is not the absence of a safety report: the rider's statement in the ticket is itself the contemporaneous report, and SAFE-1 is limited to threat/abuse keywords in chat, which was never the rider's claim.

F5 is a user-submitted statement, not a system record, and it speaks only to whether the rider complained during a 12.8-minute ride (F2) — being on the phone is entirely consistent with being too frightened to confront the driver mid-journey.

We agree no account sanction is warranted on this record — F7 shows 0 prior disputes and 0 upheld — so the rider asks only for escalation of the safety report to human handling under SAFE-2, not for any action against the driver's fare or account.

Conceded in form only: a dangerous-driving allegation does engage SAFE-2, so human review is unavoidable — but escalation under SAFE-2 is a routing of the file, not a finding of fault, and nothing in it authorises a sanction against my client.

The rider's clean 3.5-year history (F6) is a profile fact and under the policy profile facts may support an outcome but never decide the case, so it cannot convert an unevidenced allegation into an established safety incident.

Agreed, and we rely on it: with 3.6 years on the platform, 345 trips in 90 days and 0 disputes and 0 upheld disputes (F7), any escalation summary should record that there is no account-level or fare action against the driver.

The rider's own concession that the system records show a shorter-than-optimal 8.5 km run in 12.8 min versus 8.6 km / 14 min estimated (F1, F2) means there is no fare or route breach to answer, and the driver's statement (F5) stands unrefuted by any telemetry in the file.
